title: Recall Quiz: Jacobean Age & John Donne

questions.explanation: The 18th-century critic Dr. Samuel Johnson coined the term in his 'Lives of the Most Eminent English Poets'.

questions.q: In metaphysical poetry, what is a 'conceit'?
questions.explanation: A metaphysical conceit compares two vastly different things using intellect and logic.

questions.q: In which poem does Donne compare the souls of lovers to the legs of a drawing compass?
questions.explanation: This famous compass conceit is found in A Valediction: Forbidding Mourning.

questions.q: The famous line 'No man is an island' appears in which of John Donne's works?
questions.explanation: It is from his prose work, Meditation XVII, exploring the interconnectedness of humanity.

questions.q: Which poem argues that Death is merely a short sleep and will ultimately be defeated?
questions.explanation: This is the premise of Holy Sonnet 10, 'Death be not proud'.

questions.q: The publication of which major text in 1611 had a profound influence on the English language during the Jacobean era?
questions.explanation: The King James Bible was published under the sponsorship of King James I in 1611.

questions.q: Which metaphysical poet wrote the famous 'carpe diem' poem 'To His Coy Mistress'?
questions.explanation: Andrew Marvell wrote this famous poem urging his lover not to waste time.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a typical characteristic of Metaphysical poetry?
questions.explanation: Metaphysical poetry is known for its complexity, intellectual rigor, and irregular meter/rhymes, not simple predictability.
